svg.text: Risk register · initial and target risk — worksheet
risk-register.csv · generated from safety/hazards/*.yaml (initial_risk, target_risk, acceptances)
The analyst selects a severity (1–4, by the worst credible mishap) and a
probability (A–F, by likelihood over the item's life). MIL-STD-882E Table III
maps the pair to a risk level. Both selections and the stated basis are shown for
every hazard, so a reviewer can challenge the inputs, not just the result.

19 rows · mini-grid: rows A–F probability, columns 1–4 severity; outlined cell = the selection · Acceptance needs a named human reviewer in the acceptance role (rule R13); none is recorded.

g.text: Terms: 1A–4F = risk assessment code, severity 1–4 plus probability A–F (e.g. 1C) · 3D = three-dimensional · AI = artificial intelligence (here, an AI assistant drafting at independence level I0) · DoD = US Department of Defense

· F-nnn = system function in the item definition · HAZ-nnn = hazard record (safety/hazards/HAZ-xxx-nnn.yaml) · I0–I3 = review independence level (I0 none, e.g. the author or an AI, to I3 independent organisation) · MIL-STD-882E

= US DoD Standard Practice for System Safety (11 May 2012, base edition) · R01 … = validator rule in tools/pdac (R13 = only a named human review accepts anything) · RAC = risk assessment code, severity category plus probability

level (e.g. 1C) · ROLE-nnn = project role in the tailoring record (simulated until the lead says otherwise) · SUS-RISKDEF-001 = the project's tailored risk definitions (standards/tailoring) · TBD = to be determined · UAV =
uncrewed aerial vehicle (drone) · US = United States
